about: Written by hand: the workspace reorganized by one dependency-injection rule (Sam, msg 1938), with Sam's decisions on it (msgs 1939, 1952, 1978, 1979, 1981, 1984, 1986, 1987, and 2009–2022), as a transformation of the current map. propose.py applies it to map-data.js and writes proposed-data.js; it stops if a trait has no decision, or anything named here is not in the map. A chart for planning, not a change to the code. Every entry has a status: decided (by Sam) or recommended (pending Sam). Item 7, the kkt-config breakup in config-split.json, is part of the proposal, accepted by Sam (msg 1979).
rule: Every trait a crate depends on is a contract, and it is declared by its consumers, not by the crate that implements it.

If a contract is used by more than two crates, it lives in its own contract-only crate (traits, pure value types, and test doubles behind `testing`). Its real implementations live in separate implementation crates, which implement it directly (msg 2020); only programs depend on them. Model: kkt-db (contract) and kkt-db-sqlite (implementation).

For dependencies other than the named third-party wrappers below, a contract used by two crates or fewer is declared by each consumer, and the program adapts the implementation to it; the shared assembly may write an adapter the programs share.
Used by: crates other than the definer and the implementers that take the trait in a public slot or call through it, in normal dependencies. Test-only use is listed separately.

A third-party tool or library with one implementation is one crate named for the scope: its contract in the open, and the implementation, with the tool's knowledge and a private runner, behind real (phase 13, replacing phase 12's split). Several implementations, or a contract many crates share, keep a contract crate with named implementations, as kkt-service and kkt-db do. Either way the program injects the implementation, with no adapter. Language-shaping libraries retain the RUST rule 7 exemption.

new_crates.name: kkt-clock-system
new_crates.concern: The system clock and its sleep: `SystemClock`, which implements kkt-clock's `Clock` directly, a shared contract. kkt-clock's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-entropy
new_crates.concern: The randomness contract `Entropy`, with `random_chars` as a provided method that takes the alphabet to draw from, and its test doubles behind `testing`.

new_crates.name: kkt-entropy-os
new_crates.concern: Randomness from the operating system: `OsEntropy`, which implements kkt-entropy's `Entropy` directly, a shared contract. kkt-names' `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-container-docker
new_crates.concern: Docker implements Container directly; owns Docker and Compose knowledge, files, sidecar status and its private native runner, running behind real (12.2).

new_crates.name: kkt-service-os
new_crates.concern: Trying whether the service's server could listen on its address: `try_bind`, which the program passes to kkt-service's bind check. Its service files and commands went to the service manager wrappers (step 12.3).

new_crates.name: kkt-service-launchd
new_crates.concern: Implements kkt-service's Service directly as a launchd user agent on macOS: the plist, launchctl's commands and answers, the log file and the retries while launchd removes an old service, tested against a private system; the real files and commands are behind real (step 12.3, option a).

new_crates.name: kkt-service-systemd
new_crates.concern: Implements kkt-service's Service directly as a systemd user unit on Linux: the unit file, systemctl's and journalctl's commands and answers, tested against a private system; the real files and commands are behind real (step 12.3, option a).

new_crates.name: kkt-remote-access-tailscale
new_crates.concern: Implements the project's RemoteAccess contract directly; owns Tailscale arguments, parsing, messages and its private process runner behind real (step 12.1, option a).

new_crates.name: kkt-client-config-os
new_crates.concern: The machine's files and the `claude` command: `OsHost`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-client-config's `Host`. kkt-client-config's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-probe
new_crates.concern: Probing a kkt server and reading its key files: the Prober contract in the open, with KeyFile, Check, Probing, the prober's Settings and its testing stand-in, and its one implementation, HttpProber, behind real: the HTTP probe and MCP handshake with reqwest, whose types stay inside (steps 12.5b and 13.5).

new_crates.name: kkt-lane-files-os
new_crates.concern: The disk under a lane folder: `OsDisk`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-lane-files's `Disk`. The folder's git commit went to kkt-lane-commit-git (step 12.5a).

new_crates.name: kkt-lane-commit
new_crates.concern: The project's contract for the commit a lane folder is at (LaneCommit), with its testing stand-in; no tool knowledge (step 12.5a).

new_crates.name: kkt-lane-commit-git
new_crates.concern: Implements LaneCommit directly with git: its commands, what their answers mean and the wording of a failure, tested against a private runner; running git is behind real (step 12.5a, option a).

new_crates.name: kkt-web-preview
new_crates.concern: The web page over simulated data, a dev-only program with no library: kkt-web's page over kkt-api-sim's `Preview` and `PreviewGate`, which it turns kkt-api-sim's testing feature on for, with the real clock, randomness and stop signals, served alone through kkt-server's `page` and kkt-server-listen. It logs through kkt-logs-os and reads its key file through kkt-admission-os. Its flags and their checks are its own (step 6.3).

new_crates.name: kkt-server-listen
new_crates.concern: Binding the server to its socket and serving it: `listen` and `Listening`, which only the programs use. kkt-server's `real` feature moves here. It serves kkt-server's built `App`, so it needs axum.

new_crates.name: kkt-backup-os
new_crates.concern: Writing and pruning backup folders on disk: `write` and `prune`, which the program calls. kkt-backup's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-shutdown-os
new_crates.concern: The operating system's stop signals: `StopSignals`, which the programs install and which stop kkt-shutdown's `Shutdown`. kkt-shutdown's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-search
new_crates.concern: Search as text: the words of a text (FTS5 `unicode61`'s rule, with its word table), a search's terms, whether a text matches them, and an excerpt around the matches, drawn with the marks and window it is given; and `Word`. Pure text: it knows no database. kkt-db-sqlite and kkt-db's in-memory backend (behind `testing`) use it. kkt-db-sqlite's test that regenerates the word table writes to its path here, not kkt-db's search/table.rs (tests.rs:346).

new_crates.name: kkt-api-agent
new_crates.concern: What any registered agent may do, and the records every level shares: the agent's operations by area (Api, Agents, Channels, Messages, Memory, Lanes), the records, queries and errors they and the other levels use, Settings and MAX_LANE_DESCRIPTION_CHARS, `Limits`, the limits `Api::limits` reports, and `Answer`, the future every operation of the three levels returns. One of three contract crates, one per level of authority; kkt-api-operator and kkt-api-admin depend on it for the shared records. kkt-rules implements it; /mcp uses only it.

new_crates.name: kkt-api-admin
new_crates.concern: What /mcp-admin's administrator does: the 12 admin_* reads (Admin), and what is server-wide, creating a swarm (Swarms), with AdminChannel, and `AdminApi`, every operation /mcp-admin uses in one swarm: kkt-api-operator's `OperatorApi` and `Admin`, so kkt-api-admin depends on kkt-api-operator. kkt-rules implements it; kkt-mcp, for /mcp-admin, and kkt-mcp-formatter use it, and the fake product creates its second swarm through it.

new_crates.name: kkt-api-operator
new_crates.concern: What the human who runs the server may do: the web page's operator powers, by area (Views, Changes, Lanes, Server), with the records only they use (Overview, AgentActivity, ActivityCount, ChannelView, ChannelActivity, LaneHistory, StaleAgent, StaleHidden, Kept, KeptReason, ServerRunInfo, LaneSave, ChannelChange), `Notices`, the swarm's live notices that `Views::subscribe` gives, each a `Notice` with its own records (NewAgent, ChannelCreated, Joined, Left, ChannelHidden, AgentHidden, ChannelMembers; a message is kkt-api-agent's Message), and `OperatorApi`, every operation the operator may use in one swarm, the agent level's and Views included. It depends on kkt-api-agent for the shared records. kkt-rules implements it; the web page and the operator operations /mcp-admin calls use it. Open question: lanes, the server announcement and server runs are server-wide, yet its Lanes and Server traits let a swarm's operator change them; where several swarms each have an operator, changing them may belong in kkt-api-admin, with reading staying here.

new_crates.name: kkt-config-file
new_crates.concern: The config file's format: parsing its TOML into `Config`, its own record of what the file says (`parse_file`), and changing its text (`with_allowed_host`), with its own error. It reads no file and knows nothing of kkt-settings: the program turns a parsed file into kkt-settings' `ServeOptions`, and adapts it to kkt-container's parser.

new_crates.name: kkt-admission-os
new_crates.concern: The server's key files on disk: reading the access, web and admin keys and the admin name file, and writing a key file only its owner can read, new or replaced when forced, with kkt-admission's file mode. `KeyFiles` is a plain type; the programs adapt it to kkt-admission's `KeyTexts`, and kkt calls it to make and write keys, with a key factory the caller gives, so it draws no randomness of its own; a failed read is its own `ReadError`, with the file's path.

new_crates.name: kkt-setup-os
new_crates.concern: Setup's files on this machine: the setup record and its unfinished note, written whole, and kkt's data folder; this program's own path, and absolute and canonical paths; and one snapshot of `PATH`, in which it finds programs. Plain functions the program calls; the decisions are kkt-setup's. Other files go through the effect crate that owns their area: the Docker folder's through kkt-container-docker, key files through kkt-admission-os.

new_crates.name: kkt-terminal-os
new_crates.concern: The terminal: `Terminal` writes a command's output and errors, flushes a prompt, writes a watch message whole, says whether input is a terminal and, separately, whether output is, reads a line, and restores the default for a closed output pipe; `BrowserLink` shows a login link, opens it in the browser and waits for Enter. Plain types; the program adapts them to kkt-setup's `Lines`, kkt-watch's `Report` and kkt-container's `LoginLink`, and its commands write through `Terminal`.

new_crates.name: kkt-identity-keymode
new_crates.concern: Key mode's identity: `KeyMode`, which implements kkt-identity's `Identify` directly. It decides who a caller is from the key that let it in and the avatar's token, in the one swarm a key-mode server has.

new_crates.name: kkt-api-sim
new_crates.concern: A simulated application, for tests and the web preview: `Preview`, which implements the kkt-api crates' contracts over a swarm made up from a seed, answering `limits` with its own values, and `PreviewGate`, a stand-in for kkt-web's `Gate`, with an access key or open. Both are behind `testing`, with the preview's settings (`PreviewSettings`, its `SettingError`) and the viewer kkt-web's viewing test uses. Its simulated world keeps records of its own, which it translates to the kkt-api crates' records, and refuses the operations the page never asks. The preview's tests, the page scenarios over `Preview` among them, are its unit tests. kkt-web's and kkt-server's tests use it (step 6.3).

new_crates.name: kkt-config-file-os
new_crates.concern: The config file's bytes, and the instructions file's: reading and writing them whole. Plain functions the program calls; the format is kkt-config-file's.

new_crates.name: kkt-machine
new_crates.concern: Facts about the machine: `Env` (the home folder and the folders the environment names) and `Platform`, and `Machine`, which gives them, with a stand-in behind `testing`. The crates that place files on the machine take these facts; none reads them.

new_crates.name: kkt-machine-os
new_crates.concern: The machine's facts as this process sees them: `OsMachine` reads the environment and the platform, and implements kkt-machine's `Machine` directly, a shared contract. The program wires it in.

new_crates.name: kkt-hash
new_crates.concern: Hashing: `sha256`, the SHA-256 digest of some bytes. The one crate that uses sha2; its users call it.

new_crates.name: kkt-logs-os
new_crates.concern: The log's files and its start: `RotatingFile` writes the log file, and rolls it over and deletes old ones by kkt-logs' plans; `init_logging` and `init_stderr_logging` start tracing, on the terminal or in the file; `TracingLog` records kkt-log's events through tracing. kkt-logs' `real` feature moves here, with tracing-subscriber.

new_crates.name: kkt-log
new_crates.concern: Recording an event: `Log`, "record this event at this level", with `Level` (error to trace) and its named fields (`Field`, whose `Value` is formatted with Display or Debug), and a stand-in behind `testing` that captures events, as `Entry`s, for tests. A shared contract: the logic crates that log take it, and kkt-logs-os implements it.

new_crates.name: kkt-operate
new_crates.concern: The operator's commands on this machine: `kkt setup` and `kkt switch`, `kkt service`, `kkt status`, `kkt upgrade`, `kkt uninstall`, `kkt backup`, `kkt doctor`, `kkt lanes`, `kkt key` and `kkt agent`, with the setup record, the unfinished note, installs with no record, and where the operator's keys are. It takes its effects and the local server's facts in `OperateParts`, mostly as the contracts its logic crates already declare, and depends on no `-os` crate and no other assembly.

new_crates.name: kkt-agent-commands
new_crates.concern: The agents' commands: `kkt register`, `kkt reclaim`, `kkt watch` and `kkt connect`, with how a client reaches the server and the wording of what the server refuses. It takes its effects in `AgentParts`: the connection question kkt-setup declares, where the admin key is, the server's client, the credential files and the terminal. It depends on no `-os` crate, not on kkt-agent-client, and on no other assembly.

new_crates.name: kkt-agent-client-rmcp
new_crates.concern: Implements kkt-agent-client's contract directly over MCP, through rmcp and reqwest: Mcp, Client, Remote and AdminRemote, with Settings; plain Http requests for a program's test client. Everything that reaches the server is behind real (step 12.4).

new_crates.name: kkt-agent-files-os
new_crates.concern: Agent credential files and kkt watch's state files on this machine, moved from kkt-agent-client, which becomes a contract (step 12.4).

new_crates.name: kkt-client-command
new_crates.concern: The project's contract for configuring an MCP client through that client's own command line: ClientCommand, with the testing Recorder (step 12.5c).

new_crates.name: kkt-client-command-claude
new_crates.concern: Implements ClientCommand for Claude Code: claude mcp remove and add-json, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and the wording, over a private runner; running claude is behind real (step 12.5c).

new_crates.name: kkt-browser
new_crates.concern: The project's contract for opening a link in the person's browser: Browser, with the testing Recorder (step 12.5d).

new_crates.name: kkt-browser-os
new_crates.concern: Implements Browser with the system's own opener: starting it, reaping it, keeping a failure to report once; starting it is behind real (step 12.5d).

conflicts.title: Real implementations behind `real`, or in implementation crates
conflicts.text: PRINCIPLES.md rule 8 (now replaced by principles/, RUST 6) and CLAUDE.md put what touches the machine in the crate that owns the area, behind its `real` feature, and the rule moves it to implementation crates.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): each OS implementation moves to its own `*-os` crate as a plain type that implements nothing, and the consumer's `real` feature moves with it. The program writes one adapter per consumer trait: Host for kkt-container, kkt-remote-access and kkt-client-config, System, Prober and Disk.

conflicts.title: Reads and Writes: the store's contract, or the rules'
conflicts.text: Reads and Writes have one consumer, kkt-rules, so the rule has kkt-rules declare them. The plan has a second store (kkt-pro's) used through the same Reads and Writes, with the agreement test and the two-swarm test over those traits.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2017): kkt-store merges into kkt-rules. Its queries, its decisions (the swarm checks, lane version numbering, ChannelScope's translation), the core's tables and their history move into kkt-rules, which uses kkt-db directly as a consumer of a shared contract crate. Reads, Writes, the 36 copied record types, kkt-store and kkt-store-rules all go, with no adapter. Since msg 2015 showed that kkt-store decides things, A6 does not cover it. CLAUDE.md's rule that kkt-rules reaches the database only through Reads and Writes, and its kkt-store row, change with the code refactor, not in this chart.

conflicts.title: kkt-server's web adapters
conflicts.text: Step 6 made kkt-server's adapters to kkt-web's contract public, for a product that builds its own page; the rule would have the programs adapt them.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2031, changing msg 2019): kkt-web calls the kkt-api crates directly, so RulesSource and RulesSources go and the page's data needs no adapter. kkt-web's contract keeps only what is web-specific: the Gate, which kkt-server's AdmissionGate implements once for the three programs, deciding nothing (msg 2019), over kkt-web's own sessions (msg 2021). The msg 2019 reshapes land in kkt-api-agent: the limits the rules enforce in Api::limits, create_lane and update_lane in Lanes, and the operator flag in its records (A11).

conflicts.title: Who adapts OperatorWording
conflicts.text: The rule says the program adapts; kkt-format's NoticeWording is wired into the rules by kkt-server, which is not a program.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2019): as C4. kkt-server's Wording adapts kkt-names' NoticeWording to OperatorWording once, for the three programs, and hands it to the rules.

conflicts.title: The model's own traits fall below the threshold
conflicts.text: Counted by the rule, kkt-db's Backend and Evolve have no consumer besides kkt-db itself, and Connection one, so they would not get a contract crate.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2020): implementing a shared contract crate's contract is fine, just like consuming it. kkt-db is one, so kkt-db-sqlite's SqlitePlace implements Backend, Connection and Evolve directly, and kkt-db-sqlite-db and its 14-method adapter are gone.

conflicts.title: axum outside the three crates CLAUDE.md allows
conflicts.text: CLAUDE.md: axum is the HTTP framework of kkt-web, kkt-mcp and kkt-server only, and its types do not leave those three. kkt-server-listen serves the App kkt-server builds, which holds an axum Router, so it needs axum and the Router.

Changed by Sam (msg 2027): a crate or program counts as a user (consumer) of a contract only if its code calls the contract's methods. Naming a trait to wire an implementation in (for example Box<dyn watch::Server>, to pick Remote or AdminRemote), or to implement it in an adapter, is not use. Recounted from the code: the trait table lists, for each contract, the crates that only wire it in. No contract crosses the line of more than two users either way. Clock goes from 14 users to 13 (kkt-server only wires it). Entropy goes from 5 to 3 (kkt-server and the fake product only wire it), and to 5 in the proposal, so it stays a shared contract. kkt-watch's Server goes from 1 user beyond its declarer to 0 (the program only picks one): kkt-watch itself, which calls it in watch::run, is its one user, so it still declares it. kkt-admission keeps Entropy: SharedKey::generate draws new access keys with it (shared_key.rs:38), besides the session IDs that move to kkt-web.

Accepted by Sam (msg 2042): kkt-search sits in Foundations: it is pure text that the data crates build on and knows nothing of them, as kkt-clock and kkt-entropy sit under the crates that use them (msg 2014 left the layer to us).

Accepted by Sam (msg 2042): Whether a message's author, or a channel's last speaker, is the operator is part of the kkt-api records (kkt-api-agent's Message, kkt-api-operator's ChannelActivity), filled by kkt-rules, which makes the operator an actor and names it. With kkt-web rendering kkt-api-agent's records directly (msg 2031), the flag belongs with the record, not with each surface. kkt-web's live notices, which come from kkt-events, still work it out with kkt-names' is_operator.

Decided by Sam (msgs 2045 and 2052): the operations are split by who may call them, into kkt-api-agent (34), kkt-api-operator (22) and kkt-api-admin (13), each split by area. Rule used: an operation that takes an &Agent is the agent level's; one that takes an &Operator is the operator level's, or the admin's for the admin_* reads; one that takes an Actor goes by who calls it today. The ones I was unsure of, for Sam: (1) set_purpose takes an Actor; agents (channel owners) and the operator both call it, so it sits with the agent level and the operator calls it with its own authority. (2) register_with_client and reclaim_with_client are called before the caller is a registered agent; they sit with the agent level as its entry points. (3) current_server_announcement is read by every agent and by /mcp-admin; agent level. (4) subscribe is called only by the page, and hears every notice in the swarm, closed channels included; operator level. (5) Lanes, the announcement and server runs are server-wide (CLAUDE.md), which could make their changes admin; the web page's operator changes them today, so they are the operator level's, as msg 2045's examples have them. (6) save_lane, lane and lanes_page are called only by /mcp-admin, under the operator's Read and Change permissions; operator level, which /mcp-admin uses. (7) stale_agents, hide_stale_agents, hide_agent, change_channel and create_channel_as_operator are called by both the page and /mcp-admin; operator level. (8) in_swarm and limits are needed at every level; they sit in the agent level's Api, which the others depend on. (9) The shared records are in kkt-api-agent, AgentView included, since both operator (agent_view) and admin (admin_agent) return it; only ChannelActivity, StaleAgent, StaleHidden, Kept, KeptReason, ServerRunInfo, LaneSave and ChannelChange are operator-only, and AdminChannel admin-only. Sam accepted cases 1 to 4 and 6 to 9 as reasoned (msg 2052). Case 5 stays operator-level for now, to revisit (Q7).

Decided (msgs 2042 and 2045): kkt-rules' start records the run, then builds and returns the Rules; the programs call it and pass the Rules into kkt-server's Parts. record_run is not an API operation, since the run_id goes into the Deps that build the Rules (kkt-review-373, msg 2036). Creating a swarm is kkt-api-admin's Swarms::create_swarm, which the fake product calls.

status_legend: "Decided by Sam" covers the rule itself (msg 1938) and what follows from it, and Sam's rulings: msgs 1939 and 1952, the strict rule (msg 1978), and item 7, the kkt-config breakup, accepted as proposed (msg 1979); msg 1984's fixes and its items 7 and 8 (accepted in msg 1987); and the layers, kinds and kkt-format's dissolving (msgs 1981 and 1986). "Recommended, pending Sam" is what rests on an assumption, which leaves nothing pending; Q7 is a decision Sam will revisit (msg 2052). "Follows from Sam's rule" marks what the rule requires once its checks run, without a ruling of its own (msg 1992): the effects split out of kkt-server, kkt-backup and kkt-shutdown.

strict.text: No implementation implements a contract that another crate declares for itself; the program adapts (Sam, msg 1978). Implementing a shared contract crate's contract is fine, just like consuming it: the strict rule covers only consumer-declared contracts (msg 2020). The shared assembly crate kkt-server writes the adapters the three programs share, as the program would, on condition that it decides nothing (msg 2019). A crate may implement its own traits: FixedClock implements Clock, the entropy test doubles implement Entropy, kkt-db's own implementations and MemoryPlace's Evolve stay, and DryRun implements System (msg 1984; SameSource went with Sources in msg 2031). Sam rejected the refinement of msg 1952, which let an implementation implement its one consumer's contract directly, because it leads to tight coupling. Sam amended this for third-party tools and libraries in phase 12: always a scope contract and named wrapper, implementing it directly. The program only injects; tool knowledge and the private runner live together in the effect wrapper, running behind real.

renames.concern: The MCP tools' results turned into text or JSON, within the response size cap: `Formatter`, `Format`, its `Settings` and `MIN_RESPONSE_BYTES`. It is what was left of kkt-format, which is dissolved; `NoticeWording` moved to kkt-rules, as its default wording.

kkt-clock.concern: Time: the `Clock` contract, kkt's time types `Time` and `Span`, the time text functions, and `FixedClock` behind `testing`. Contract-only: its real clock is in kkt-clock-system. The only crate that uses chrono.

kkt-names.concern: Avatars' handles, channel IDs, the name packs, and the operator and admin names with their rules. It draws randomness through kkt-entropy's `Entropy`, with its own character sets.

kkt-rules.concern: Every permission decision and every change, for agents and the operator, each in one swarm: it is the implementation of the application's shared contracts, kkt-api-agent, kkt-api-operator and kkt-api-admin, through Rules, and provides the default wording, DefaultWording, as its own OperatorWording. Its `start` records a server run, then builds the Rules from a `Startup`, the rules' `Deps` without the run. It holds the core's data privately: its queries as kkt-db operations on a Db it is given, the core's tables as migrations with their history from before kkt-db, and the check that swarms stay apart. kkt-store merged into it; the database stays private.
kkt-rules.must_not: Name a database or use a database library: it reaches the database through kkt-db's contract, which the program fills with the SQLite backend.

kkt-db-sqlite.concern: SQLite, the only crate that knows it: it opens a SQLite database, in a file or in memory, adopts a database from before kkt-db by SQLite's `user_version`, and copies one for backups. SqlitePlace implements kkt-db's Backend, Connection and Evolve directly, since kkt-db is a shared contract crate, and runs the blocking work on tokio's blocking pool.

kkt-db.concern: The database contract, for any database: values, tables, keys and constraints; a narrow language of questions and changes (not SQL), with Schema's checks of which are valid; transactions, through Backend and the typed read and write BackendExt provides; search's Search and Hit; migrations as additions, run by Evolve's provided migrate and pending; the shape of a database from before kkt-db; and its own in-memory backend and fault-injecting backend behind `testing`. Every behaviour is a method of its own traits and types. kkt-db-sqlite implements it directly, as a shared contract.

kkt-server.concern: Assembling the server from its parts and running it: the rules, `/mcp`, `/mcp-admin` and the web page. Its parts take the application that kkt-rules' `start` built as one `Arc<dyn AdminApi>`, which each surface takes as its own contract, and one value meeting kkt-identity's `Identify`, which it hands to the endpoints and its web gate asks. It writes the adapters the three programs share, once, and decides nothing: AdmissionGate implements kkt-web's Gate. It builds the page's sessions and page-only limits, and `page` builds the web page alone, over any `OperatorApi` and gate, for a program that serves only the page (kkt-web-preview). Binding the socket is in kkt-server-listen. It holds `ServerSettings`, the settings of what it builds or passes on, each an owner's own `Settings`, and puts in a fixed order the problems and run-record lines that the owners and the program give it. It knows nothing of flags, files or how they layer.

kkt-agent-client.concern: The shared MCP client for agent commands: avatar credentials and their files on disk (read with their owner and mode, which the caller's `CredentialCheck` judges as named `CredentialFileFacts`, and made private as its `PrivateMode` says, with warnings through the caller's callbacks; in kkt the check is kkt-setup's rule), watch's state file and its lock, reaching the server as an agent or admin through plain methods with its own types, and plain HTTP for probes. It knows nothing of kkt-watch; the program adapts it.

kkt-mcp.concern: The agent and admin MCP tools, what the two share, their HTTP transport, and what agents are told about each tool. It calls the kkt-api crates directly and depends on no kkt-rules type: kkt-api-agent's `Api` for /mcp, and for /mcp-admin kkt-api-admin's `AdminApi`, which includes the operator operations it offers. It declares the `Identify` it asks; kkt-server hands it the program's adapter.

kashkeshet.concern: The `kkt` command: parsing its arguments, wiring the crates together for each subcommand, and one thin module per command. It does no machine work itself: files, keys, credentials, the terminal, the environment and the log go through effect crates, and the decisions its commands made are kkt-setup's and kkt-service's. It holds the adapters the strict rule needs: one per consumer-declared contract it fills with another crate's implementation (kkt-agent-client's watching and state file, the key files, the terminal and the six -os crates). Shared contracts' implementations need none, and kkt-server writes the web page's and the wording's adapters for it. It keeps `kkt serve`'s surface: its flags and config keys, layering flag over file over the defaults, and mapping each onto a `ServerSettings` field or a setting of its own. It composes the server itself (`kkt serve`: the settings, the keys, the database, starting the rules and listening, over kkt-server). Its other commands are two assemblies, kkt-operate and kkt-agent-commands; it keeps the command line (`cli.rs`), `main.rs`, which builds each assembly's `Parts` from the implementations it chooses, and the adapters, and answers each assembly's questions about the local server from its serving code.
kashkeshet.must_not: Do machine work itself (files, the terminal, the environment, the log, libc); hold a decision a logic crate owns; hold a clap type outside `cli.rs`, or let a command take one.

kkt-keymode.concern: A second program that assembles key mode again from the shared crates with none of the `kkt` program's code, with its own adapters, as the strict rule has every program write, and the shared store and database adapters. Its key files, terminal and settings checks are the shared crates' too. The HTTP-only end-to-end tests run against it in CI. Dev-only, never released.
kkt-keymode.must_not: Do machine work itself: files, the terminal and the log go through the effect crates.

kkt-fake-product.concern: The shared crates assembled as a product other than kkt would assemble them, with two swarms and `FakeIdentify`, which implements kkt-identity's `Identify`. It adapts the implementations it wires, as every program does, and takes the shared database adapter. It does no machine work itself; the HTTP client its tests use is in its tests. Its tests check that nothing of one swarm reaches the other. Dev-only, never released.
kkt-fake-product.must_not: Do machine work itself: files, the terminal and the log go through the effect crates.

kkt-admission.concern: Whether an HTTP caller is let in at all, and as which `Principal`: no key, which of the server's keys, or (for another program's `Identify` to judge) any bearer token. Also the checks on the server's keys, and which admin name a key carries (`server_keys::bound_to`, `bound_in`). The web page's sessions are kkt-web's; for the page it answers whether sign-in is needed, whether a key is good and whom it admits.

kkt-container.concern: Container operations, requests and results in project terms; config parsing and login-link contracts; a testing stand-in.
kkt-container.must_not: Know Docker commands, Compose files or their formats; touch the machine.

kkt-service.concern: The project's contract for running kkt as a service of the user's login (Service), its values and errors, Unsupported for other systems, and the service plan and bind check on plain values; its testing stand-in. No service manager's knowledge.

kkt-remote-access.concern: The project's sharing contract RemoteAccess, Node and its testing stand-in; no tool knowledge.

kkt-client-config.concern: MCP client configs and their file formats, so `kkt connect` can add kkt to a client. It declares the `Host` it works through; the real one is in kkt-client-config-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-diagnostics.concern: `kkt doctor`'s checks and their plan, and setup's wait for a new server. It checks through kkt-probe's `Prober`, which the program injects.

kkt-lane-files.concern: Lanes as files: the `<lane>.md` format, and reading and writing a folder of them, with the commit it is at from kkt-lane-commit's LaneCommit. It declares the `Disk` it works through; the real one is in kkt-lane-files-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-web.concern: The human's pages, over the application's operations: it calls kkt-api-agent and kkt-api-operator directly and renders their records. Its own contract keeps only what is web-specific: `Gate` says whether a key lets a viewer in and who a viewer is, as a `Viewer` record (a swarm and an operator); the page takes the application as one `OperatorApi` and calls it in each viewer's swarm. It keeps the sign-in sessions and form tokens itself (`Sessions`, generic over what the gate says a key admits, and told by its `Access` whether sign-in is required), with their lifetime in its `Settings`, the page-only limits (`PageLimits`, its `Settings`' `page`), and its live updates, which it draws from kkt-api-operator's `Notices` and serializes itself. The page scenarios every implementation must pass (`testing`, over a `testing::App`).
kkt-web.must_not: Depend on the rules, the store, admission or identity, or on an implementation crate: it uses the agent and operator levels' contracts, and kkt-server implements its Gate.

kkt-events.concern: Notices of new messages, agents, channels and members, and of hidden agents and channels: one bus for the server, each notice heard only in its swarm, with a buffer per swarm kept only while it has a subscriber. The buffer's size is a setting the program fills.

kkt-watch.concern: `kkt watch`: waiting for an agent's new messages (or every channel's, as admin) and the line printed for each. The server, clock, saved place, output and its retry and wait timings are injected by the program.

kkt-backup.concern: Backup folders: their names, what goes in them and their file modes, and which to prune; the disk work is in kkt-backup-os.

kkt-shutdown.concern: The stop signal: `Shutdown`, whose clones share one signal. The operating system's signals are in kkt-shutdown-os.

kkt-logs.concern: The log's rules and settings: `LogLevel` and `LogPolicy` with their checks and its own `SettingError`, and the plans for the files: when the file rolls over and which renames that takes (`should_roll`, `rotation`), and when to look for old rolled files and which to delete (`prune_due`, `pruning`). It touches no file: kkt-logs-os carries out the plans.

kkt-setup.concern: `kkt setup`: what this machine is set up as, the setup record, and what follows from it: whether `kkt serve` may run here, which server and key this machine's clients use (`kkt switch`; `connection`, over the reads its `ConnectionSource` asks for in their original order), how setup asks its questions (its `Prompter` over its own `Lines`), and what status, upgrade, uninstall, lanes, backup, key files and `kkt doctor` decide: the status lines, the backup folders, the record uninstall leaves, the per-server client key's name, the lane limit, the import report, and the doctor's checks and fixes as plain `DoctorCheck`s, which the program adapts to kkt-diagnostics' report. It reads no files and runs nothing: the program does, through the effect crates, and carries out what is decided here.

kkt-identity.concern: Who a caller is: `Identify`, the one contract kkt-mcp's endpoints and kkt-server's web gate ask (which avatar a call acts as, the swarm a newcomer joins, which operator a principal is), with `Identified` and `Identifying`, and a stand-in behind `testing`. kkt-web-preview.concern: The web preview program: it serves kkt-web's page over kkt-api-sim's simulated application, from flags (the address, the seed and the preview's settings). A dev-only program that turns kkt-api-sim's testing feature on, since dev tooling counts as test code.

kkt-container-docker.concern: Docker and Compose implement Container directly, including their files, commands, output and sidecar status; native execution is behind real.
kkt-container-docker.must_not: Decide setup answers or remember the setup record.

page_rules: Every trait a crate depends on is a contract, declared by the crates that use it, not by the crate that implements it. A crate uses a contract when its code calls the contract's methods; naming a trait only to wire an implementation in, or to implement it, is not use.

A contract used by more than two crates lives in a contract-only crate of its own (traits, plain value types with pure behaviour on them, and test doubles behind `testing`). Any crate may implement a shared contract crate's contract directly. Model: kkt-db (contract) and kkt-db-sqlite (implementation).

For dependencies other than named third-party wrappers, a contract used by two crates or fewer is declared by each consumer. The program adapts the implementation; kkt-server may share those adapters between its programs.
A crate may implement its own traits (FixedClock implements Clock, DryRun implements System).

Each crate is one kind, by what it does: contract, contract and effect, logic, effect, composition or test support. Only programs and compositions depend on effect crates, only programs turn on a contract-and-effect crate's real (check 2), and no crate mixes logic or a contract with an effect. Named tool wrappers are the explicit exception: effect crates also hold tool knowledge, tested through a private runner (phase 12, option a). A contract-and-effect crate is not mixed: its effect is its own contract's one implementation, behind real (phase 13).

The application's operations are three contract crates, one per level of authority: kkt-api-agent (what any registered agent may do, and the shared records), kkt-api-operator (what the human who runs the server may do) and kkt-api-admin (what the administrator does). kkt-rules implements all three.

A third-party tool or library with one implementation is one crate named for the scope: its contract in the open, and the implementation, with the tool's knowledge and a private runner, behind real (phase 13, replacing phase 12's split). Several implementations, or a contract many crates share, keep a contract crate with named implementations, as kkt-service and kkt-db do. Either way the program injects the implementation, with no adapter. Language-shaping libraries retain the RUST rule 7 exemption.
